First, let $u=-4-2x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4}{-4-2x}\,\text{d}x & =4\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot\left(-\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u\right) \\ & =-2\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\ & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\ & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|-4-2x|+C\end{aligned}
$$
